subject: Urgent: batch/cache feedback loop causing customer impact — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: support@brightbyte.io
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Batch/cache feedback loop causing latency spikes (Brightbyte)

Hi Tom / Brightbyte ops,

We're seeing a repeatable customer-impacting pattern on your production workload this morning: p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s across the last 45 minutes, error-rate (5xx) increased from 0.1% -> 2.8%, and throughput dropped by ~30%. Our initial traces point to HOL (head-of-line) blocking inside the priority lane and aggressive KV cache eviction behavior that is thrashing the prefetched keyset for your tenant.

Key observations so far (attached CSV + log snippet):
- Start: 08:26 PDT — coordinated small spike that escalated; continuous oscillation thereafter.
- KV cache eviction rate up 7x vs baseline; many short-lived keys re-prefetched.
- Batching backlog observed on two GPU hosts servicing the tenant (batch lane backlog + waiting requests).

Immediate ask: can we get a 30-60 minute war room to triage? We propose the following short-term mitigations while we investigate:
1) Temporarily backoff priority-lane concurrency for Brightbyte (reduce to 60% of normal)
2) Increase KV cache TTL for the tenant by 2x to reduce churn
3) Enable conservative batching mode on the two affected hosts (reduce max batch size from 128 -> 64)

I've attached a snapshot of the metrics and a brief log extract. If you prefer a call, please propose a time in the next 20 minutes.

Sorry for the disruption — we want to prioritize this for Brightbyte.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-22T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Batch/cache feedback loop causing latency spikes — rapid remediation steps

Kim / team — putting a quick runbook together. TL;DR: we need to (A) stabilize traffic, (B) reduce KV churn, (C) run a short canary for routing change. Proposed immediate steps (15-30 min):
- Ops: add a temporary tenant throttle at the edge (limit inflight per connection to 8) — reduces HOL pressure.
- Runtime: flip KV TTL for Brightbyte to 2x (config flag) — reduces re-insertion churn.
- Serving: reduce max_batch_size to 64 on the two affected instances and set batching_policy=conservative.
- Escalation: request marissa_cole for exec sync (we may need to offer credits if this hits SLA).

Jonas, can you lead the runtime patch + canary? I'll coordinate comms with Brightbyte and own the customer-facing updates.

-Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Batch/cache feedback loop 

Thanks — quick technical readout from logs and traces:
- Root contributor: a narrow set (~120) of hot keys for Brightbyte exhibits bursty write/read patterns. Prefetching was aggressively re-inserting keys with TTL=10s; eviction churn caused repeated misses and re-prefetch -> increases KV write amplification.
- HOL blocking observed when a large request enters the priority lane and waits behind a long tail response; that stalls batch formation across lanes, causing other requests to queue and timeout.
- We also see misrouting events where prefetched keys were written to a non-local shard due to a transient routing map update — those caused additional cross-host fetches and amplified latency.

Immediate technical mitigations I can push now (I will coordinate a canary):
1) KV TTL bump for tenant config (10s -> 30s) — low risk; reduces churn.
2) Disable aggressive background prefetcher for the tenant for 30 minutes.
3) Apply a hotkey pinning override to force hot keys to local shards for Brightbyte for the next 60 minutes.
4) Route-level concurrency cap: max_inflight=8 for priority lane to avoid HOL cascade.

I'll roll 1+2 in the next 7 minutes to the canary group (one host) and monitor. If stable at 5 minutes, I'll roll to the remaining host.

-Jonas
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, tom.reynolds@brightbyte.io
Date: 2026-10-22T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: batch/cache feedback loop causing customer impact — exec attention requested

Marissa — fwding the full thread and attachments (metrics + logs + temp playbook). Summary for leadership:
- Impact: Brightbyte production experienced sustained p95 latency ~1.2s, increased error-rate, and degraded throughput for ~2 hours. This kicked off at 08:26 PDT and persisted through operator mitigations.
- Cause (current assessment): compounded effect of aggressive prefetch + short KV TTL leading to eviction/reprefetch cycles, plus routing map miswrites that produced cross-host fetch amplification. HOL blocking on the priority lane amplified tail latency and led to request timeouts.
- Actions taken: throttled priority lane, bumped KV TTL (10s->30s) in canary then full roll, disabled aggressive prefetch, applied hotkey pin override, reduced batch size to 64 on affected hosts.
- Current state: after full roll, p95 reduced to ~220ms and error-rate trending down to baseline (0.3%). Monitoring for 1 hour before closing.
- Customer asks: confirmation on data staleness impact (they flagged 30s requirement), and SLA credit conversation.

Requested leadership decisions:
1) Approve initial goodwill credit (recommended 5% of monthly invoice) pending final postmortem.
2) Approve immediate follow-up with product to add a tenant-level prefetch control and hotkey pin policy (product ticket RW-4521 linked).
3) Authorize a joint postmortem with Brightbyte and a single-page executive summary for their customers.

I'll schedule a 30-min briefing in the next hour for execs and product.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
